query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small amount of Sn to single‐phase fcc FeCoNi alloys will induce the formation of nano‐scale BCC precipitates, and the resulting dual-phase microstructure will pin domain walls more effectively, increasing the coercive field beyond the typical <100 Oe observed in the pure fcc system.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi (or a closely derived high-entropy alloy) with saturation magnetization in the high range and coercivity below 100 Oe.
generation.intervention: Introduce a controlled Sn addition (e.g., by alloying during vacuum arc-melting) to the FeCoNi system so as to promote a secondary, minor BCC phase formation.
generation.conditions: Alloys prepared by standard melting (e.g., vacuum arc-melting) and subsequent controlled annealing to allow phase separation; magnetic measurements performed at or near room temperature.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of nano-scale BCC precipitates (or an incipient dual-phase structure) embedded in the fcc matrix.
generation.mechanism: The nano-scale BCC precipitates and the associated phase boundaries act as effective pinning centers for magnetic domain walls, leading to an elevated coercive field relative to the single-phase fcc alloy.
generation.predicted_outcome: A measurable increase in coercivity (exceeding 100 Oe) relative to the baseline single-phase fcc FeCoNi, with saturation magnetization remaining comparably high.
generation.baseline: Pure single-phase fcc FeCoNi or its derivatives, which exhibit low coercivity (<100 Oe) in standard magnetic measurements.
generation.boundary: The intervention is effective if the Sn concentration is optimized to induce the formation of a dual-phase microstructure without significantly compromising the high saturation magnetization. Measurements and phase analyses are conducted at room temperature under comparable processing conditions.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal Sn concentration and the precise magnitude of coercivity increase are uncertain and would require experimental calibration.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a series of FeCoNi alloys with incremental Sn additions (e.g., 0, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10 atomic fraction) under identical melting and annealing conditions. Characterize the phase constitution with X-ray diffraction and electron microscopy, and measure the magnetic hysteresis loops (coercivity and saturation magnetization) using a vibrating sample magnetometer at room temperature.
measurements: XRD to detect the presence of BCC phase (or secondary phase peaks)
TEM/SEM for microstructural confirmation of nano-scale precipitates
Magnetic hysteresis measurements (coercivity Hc, saturation magnetization Ms)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Sn addition does not result in the formation of a secondary phase or nano-scale precipitates (as determined by XRD and microscopy) and/or there is no statistically significant increase in coercivity (i.e., coercivity remains ≤100 Oe) compared to the control alloy, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: The present work exhibits the effects of Sn addition on the magnetic properties and microstructure of FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) high-entropy alloys (HEAs). The results show all the samples consist of a mixed structure of face-centered-cubic (FCC) phase and body-centered-cubic (BCC) phase. The addition of Sn promotes the formation of BCC phase, and it also affects the shape of Cu-rich nano-precipitates in BCC matrix. It also shows that the Curie temperatures (Tc) of the FCC phase and the saturation magnetization (Ms) of the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs increase greatly while the remanence (Br) decreases after the addition of Sn into FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 HEA. The thermomagnetic curves indicate that the phases of the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs will transform from FCC with low Tc to BCC phase with high Tc at temperature of 600–700 K. This work provides a new idea for FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs for their potential application as soft magnets to be used at high temperatures.

In this work, the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs were prepared by vacuum arc-melt casting. Effects of Sn content on the phase constitution and magnetic properties were studied. All the samples are composed of FCC and BCC phases, whereas some unknown phases appear with the addition of Sn. The addition of Sn promotes the formation of BCC phase, and it also affects the shape of Cu-rich nanoprecipitates in the BCC matrix. Moreover, the Ms increases greatly while the remanence (Br) decreases with the increasing of x for FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs. The addition of Sn can obviously increase the Curie temperature of the FCC phase. The phase of alloys with a mixture of FCC and BCC will transform from FCC to BCC phase at high temperature, leading to an increase of magnetization. They can be used as new soft magnetic materials at high temperatures.
